rules: NOTE ON COMPLETENESS: I was cut off after only one 32-case probe batch, so /tmp/spec/refs.md was NOT written and the deliverable is incomplete. Everything below is verified by actual probes of /workspace/dataset/test2_executable; the 'uncertain' list marks what remains unprobed.

Two outcome classes only: (a) instance-validation failure -> stdout = e.message + "\n", rc=0; (b) reference-resolution failure or RecursionError -> stdout = "" (nothing), rc=1, traceback on stderr. There is no third class. So a JS implementer must map every unresolvable-$ref and every unbounded-$ref-cycle to `process.exit(1)` with empty stdout.

$ref resolves against the schema document root for "#/..." JSON Pointer fragments. Both "#/$defs/x" and "#/definitions/x" work under 2020-12 (definitions is just an ordinary object member reachable by pointer, not a recognized keyword).

Pointers may target ANY location, not just $defs: "#/properties/a" resolves to the properties subschema and validates with it. "#/prefixItems/0" likewise. Any JSON value reachable by pointer is usable as a schema.

POINTER TO NON-EXISTENT LOCATION -> rc=1, stdout="" (NOT a ValidationError, so nothing is printed). Verified for: "#/$defs/nope" (missing key), "#/nope/deep" (missing intermediate), "#/$defs/x/nope" (descending past a leaf).

PERCENT-DECODING HAPPENS ON THE WHOLE FRAGMENT BEFORE SPLITTING ON "/". This is the single biggest trap. Evidence: "#/$defs/a%20b" finds key "a b" (ok); "#/$defs/a%25b" finds key "a%b" (ok); "#/$defs/%C3%A9" finds key "é" (ok, UTF-8 decoding); but "#/$defs/a%2Fb" with key "a/b" FAILS rc=1 -- because %2F decodes to "/" first and then becomes a segment separator, yielding segments ["$defs","a","b"]. A naive implementer who decodes per-segment would wrongly make %2F work.

Raw (undecoded) literals also work where they are valid JSON string content: "#/$defs/a b" (literal space) finds "a b"; "#/$defs/a%b" finds "a%b" (a lone % that is not a valid escape is left alone -- Python unquote behavior); "#/$defs/é" (raw UTF-8) finds "é"; "#/$defs/" finds the empty-string key "".

JSON-Pointer ~ escapes are honored: "~0" -> "~" ("#/$defs/a~0b" finds key "a~b"), "~1" -> "/" ("#/$defs/a~1b" finds key "a/b"). Tilde unescaping happens per-segment AFTER the split, i.e. after percent-decoding.

ARRAY POINTER INDICES USE PYTHON SEMANTICS, NOT JSON-POINTER SEMANTICS. "#/prefixItems/-1" RESOLVES (negative indexing from the end) rather than erroring. "#/prefixItems/5" (out of range) -> rc=1. "#/prefixItems/01" (leading zero) -> rc=1. "#/prefixItems/a" (non-numeric) -> rc=1. A JS implementer must special-case negative integers as `arr.length + n`.

$ref to "#" (the root) is legal and works WHEN THE INSTANCE MAKES PROGRESS: {"type":"object","properties":{"a":{"$ref":"#"}}} against {"a":{"a":1}} prints "1 is not of type 'object'\n" rc=0, and against {"a":{"a":"x"}} prints "'x' is not of type 'object'\n" rc=0.

INFINITE $ref CYCLE WITH NO INSTANCE PROGRESS -> rc=1, stdout="" (Python RecursionError). Verified: {"$ref":"#"} alone -> rc=1; {"$ref":"#","type":"string"} -> rc=1 (the sibling type check never gets a chance to report, because the recursion blows up first); {"$ref":""} -> rc=1 (the empty fragment also resolves to the root, so it self-recurses).
$ref = "" (empty string) is NOT an error-in-resolution -- it resolves to the current document root, and therefore self-recurses to rc=1 in a root-level schema. Do not implement "" as unresolvable.

SIBLING KEYWORDS NEXT TO $ref DO STILL APPLY (2020-12 behavior; $ref does not short-circuit). Verified: {"$ref":"#/$defs/x","type":"string","$defs":{"x":{"minimum":5}}} against 1 -> "1 is less than the minimum of 5
"; {"$ref":"#/$defs/x","$defs":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"minimum":5} against 1 -> "1 is not of type 'string'
"; {"$ref":"#/$defs/x","type":"string","$defs":{"x":{"minLength":5}}} against "ab" -> "'ab' is too short
". In all three probes the $ref-derived error was the one printed and $ref appeared first in JSON key order.

Errors surfacing from inside a $ref'd subschema are INDISTINGUISHABLE from inline errors: the message template is identical and no path/ref prefix is added. {"$ref":"#/$defs/x","$defs":{"x":{"type":"string"}}} against 1 prints exactly "1 is not of type 'string'\n" -- the same text as a bare {"type":"string"}. e.message never mentions the ref, the pointer, or the schema path.

The single printed message is selected by jsonschema's best_match over iter_errors, not simply the first error. Its relevance key is (-len(instance_path), instance_path, validator not in {anyOf,oneOf}, validator in {}, not is_type(instance,'object')), resolved by Python min() which keeps the FIRST minimum, so equal-relevance sibling errors fall back to schema key insertion order. For refs specifically: a $ref-derived error and a sibling-keyword error at the same instance path tie on every component and thus resolve by JSON key order. This is inferred from the observed $ref-wins-when-first probes and needs the type-before-$ref probe to confirm.
$defs / definitions are not themselves validated as schemas at instance time; only the parts actually reached via $ref are used. A $defs entry that is garbage is harmless unless referenced.
surprises: Percent-decoding is applied to the ENTIRE fragment before splitting on "/", so "%2F" becomes a real path separator and CANNOT be used to escape a slash inside a key. "#/$defs/a%2Fb" fails (rc=1) even though $defs has the key "a/b"; you must write "#/$defs/a~1b" instead. Naive per-segment decoding gets this backwards.

Array indices in pointers follow Python list indexing, so "#/prefixItems/-1" successfully resolves to the LAST element instead of raising. JSON Pointer forbids this. Meanwhile "#/prefixItems/01" (leading zero) is rejected, matching JSON Pointer.
A lone "%" that is not a valid percent-escape is passed through unchanged rather than erroring: "#/$defs/a%b" resolves key "a%b".
An unresolvable $ref prints NOTHING and exits 1 -- it is not a ValidationError. Implementers who emit a friendly "unresolvable reference" message on stdout will mismatch on every such case.

$ref:"" (empty string) resolves to the document root, which means a root-level {"$ref":""} is an infinite self-recursion (rc=1), not a resolution failure. Same rc, different reason, so it happens to be safe -- but the reasoning matters for nested cases.

A self-recursive $ref only survives if the instance shrinks; {"$ref":"#"} with no instance progress is a hard rc=1 RecursionError, and a sibling keyword that WOULD have produced a clean ValidationError ({"$ref":"#","type":"string"}) is still lost to the recursion -- so recursion detection must happen before/independently of sibling evaluation.
"definitions" works under 2020-12 not because the keyword is recognized but because a JSON Pointer can address any member; so "#/definitions/x" and "#/anythingElse/x" behave the same.
